```{r setup, include=FALSE}
matrix_cells <- function(values) {
    stopifnot(is.matrix(values), !is.null(rownames(values)),
        !is.null(colnames(values)))
    data.frame(
        feature = factor(rep(rownames(values), ncol(values)),
            levels = rev(rownames(values))),
        sample = factor(rep(colnames(values), each = nrow(values)),
            levels = colnames(values)),
        value = as.vector(values)
    )
}
heatmap_theme <- ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#F2F2F2", colour = NA),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
    )
draw_heatmap_pair <- function(left, right) {
    panels <- lapply(list(left, right), ggplot2::ggplotGrob)
    heights <- grid::unit.pmax(panels[[1L]]$heights, panels[[2L]]$heights)
    grid::grid.newpage()
    grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(1L, 2L)))
    for (index in seq_along(panels)) {
        panels[[index]]$heights <- heights
        grid::grid.draw(grid::grobTree(panels[[index]],
            vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1L, layout.pos.col = index)))
    }
    grid::popViewport()
}
```

# Introduction

GeneFunnel turns a non-negative feature-by-sample matrix into a
gene-set-by-sample score matrix. It preserves observed magnitude while
penalizing absolute variation among the available members of each set. Every
gene set and sample is calculated independently.

Transcriptomic and proteomic assays commonly use Bioconductor's matrix,
sparse-matrix, and parallel infrastructure. GeneFunnel fits that environment by
accepting base and `Matrix` matrices and a `BiocParallelParam`, while returning
a plain numeric matrix for downstream analysis. It is a scorer only: it does
not normalize data, impute missing values, map identifiers, retrieve gene sets,
or perform statistical testing.

Within a larger pipeline, GeneFunnel can follow assay-specific preprocessing,
identifier mapping, and coverage checks. Its output can then provide
gene-set-level features for sample prioritization, visualization, clustering, or
statistical models.

The package is in development and has not been accepted into Bioconductor. Its
source and issue tracker are on the
[GeneFunnel repository](https://github.com/eturkes/genefunnel).

# Installation

After acceptance, install GeneFunnel from a Bioconductor package repository:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("genefunnel")
```

During review, replace the package name with `"eturkes/genefunnel"` to install
the development repository.

Load the installed package and choose a serial backend for the first examples.

```{r load}
library(genefunnel)
serial <- BiocParallel::SerialParam()
```

# How the score is calculated

For one declared gene set, GeneFunnel first deduplicates member identifiers and
matches them exactly and case-sensitively to matrix row names. Within sample
$j$, it omits matched values that are `NA` or `NaN`. If the remaining observed
values are $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ and $n \ge 2$, the score is

$$
\bar{x}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{GeneFunnel}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)
=\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i
-\frac{n}{2(n-1)}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|x_i-\bar{x}|.
$$

The cell is `NA_real_` when fewer than two observed members remain. Zero is an
observed value, including an implicit sparse zero, so it participates in $n$,
the sum, the mean, and the deviation. Infinities and negative values are
invalid.

The controlled panel below follows the exploratory logic used to motivate the
method. It holds total signal constant while changing within-set dispersion, and
it distinguishes observed zeros from unavailable measurements.

# Controlled expression patterns

Ten features form two five-member modules and one broader program. The six
samples represent deliberately different expression patterns rather than
biological replicates.

```{r controlled-patterns}
pattern_assay <- rbind(
    gene_A = c(38, 0, 80, 80, 80, 80),
    gene_B = c(41, 0, 80, 80, 80, 0),
    gene_C = c(39, 92, 80, 80, 80, 0),
    gene_D = c(42, 4, 80, 80, 80, 0),
    gene_E = c(40, 112, 80, 80, 80, 0),
    gene_F = c(37, 82, 80, NA, 0, 0),
    gene_G = c(43, 5, 80, NA, 0, 0),
    gene_H = c(40, 18, 80, NA, 0, 0),
    gene_I = c(41, 85, 80, NA, 0, 0),
    gene_J = c(39, 2, 80, NA, 0, 0)
)
colnames(pattern_assay) <- c(
    "coherent",
    "same_total_dispersed",
    "uniform_high",
    "partial_observation",
    "half_active",
    "single_driver"
)
pattern_sets <- list(
    module_A = rownames(pattern_assay)[1:5],
    module_B = rownames(pattern_assay)[6:10],
    broad_program = rownames(pattern_assay)
)
pattern_scores <- genefunnel(
    pattern_assay,
    pattern_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)

knitr::kable(
    pattern_assay,
    digits = 0,
    col.names = c(
        "Coherent",
        "Same total, dispersed",
        "Uniform high",
        "Partial observation",
        "Half active",
        "Single driver"
    )
)
```

```{r controlled-pattern-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.cap=pattern_heatmap_caption}
pattern_heatmap <- data.frame(
    feature = rep(rownames(pattern_assay), times = ncol(pattern_assay)),
    pattern = rep(colnames(pattern_assay), each = nrow(pattern_assay)),
    value = as.vector(pattern_assay),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
pattern_heatmap$feature <- factor(
    pattern_heatmap$feature,
    levels = rev(rownames(pattern_assay))
)
pattern_heatmap$pattern <- factor(
    pattern_heatmap$pattern,
    levels = colnames(pattern_assay)
)
pattern_labels <- c(
    coherent = "Coherent",
    same_total_dispersed = "Same total,\ndispersed",
    uniform_high = "Uniform\nhigh",
    partial_observation = "Partial\nobservation",
    half_active = "Half\nactive",
    single_driver = "Single\ndriver"
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    pattern_heatmap,
    ggplot2::aes(x = pattern, y = feature, fill = value)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        data = pattern_heatmap[is.na(pattern_heatmap$value), , drop = FALSE],
        mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = pattern, y = feature),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        shape = 4,
        size = 2.1,
        stroke = 0.7,
        colour = "#555555"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = pattern_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
        low = "#F7FBFF",
        high = "#08519C",
        na.value = "#E0E0E0",
        name = "Observed\nvalue"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Feature") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
        legend.position = "right"
    )
```

The following diagnostics expose the calculation for the broad program. The
scaled deviation is the complete penalty subtracted from the observed total.

```{r controlled-pattern-diagnostics}
pattern_diagnostics <- t(vapply(
    seq_len(ncol(pattern_assay)),
    function(column_index) {
        observed <- pattern_assay[, column_index]
        observed <- observed[!is.na(observed)]
        member_count <- length(observed)
        total <- sum(observed)
        average <- mean(observed)
        scaled_deviation <- member_count / (2 * (member_count - 1)) *
            sum(abs(observed - average))

        c(
            observed_members = member_count,
            total = total,
            mean = average,
            scaled_deviation = scaled_deviation,
            genefunnel_score =
                pattern_scores["broad_program", column_index]
        )
    },
    numeric(5L)
))
pattern_diagnostics <- data.frame(
    pattern = colnames(pattern_assay),
    pattern_diagnostics,
    check.names = FALSE
)
rownames(pattern_diagnostics) <- NULL
knitr::kable(
    pattern_diagnostics,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
        "Pattern",
        "Observed members",
        "Total",
        "Mean",
        "Scaled deviation",
        "GeneFunnel score"
    )
)

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
    unname(pattern_scores["broad_program", ]),
    c(3530 / 9, 1490 / 9, 800, 400, 1600 / 9, 0),
    tolerance = 1e-10
)))
```

```{r pattern-components, echo=FALSE, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap=components_cap}
pattern_calculation <- pattern_diagnostics
pattern_calculation$pattern <- factor(
    pattern_calculation$pattern,
    levels = colnames(pattern_assay)
)
pattern_calculation$annotation <- sprintf(
    "n = %d\nTotal = %.0f\nMean = %.1f\nPenalty = %.1f",
    pattern_calculation$observed_members,
    pattern_calculation$total,
    pattern_calculation$mean,
    pattern_calculation$scaled_deviation
)
ggplot2::ggplot(
    pattern_calculation,
    ggplot2::aes(x = pattern, y = 1, fill = genefunnel_score)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(height = 0.9, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", genefunnel_score),
            colour = genefunnel_score > 450),
        size = 3.4, fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(y = -0.55, label = annotation),
        colour = "#222222", size = 3.1, lineheight = 1.15
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "white"),
        guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = pattern_labels, position = "top") +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(-1.8, 1.6), breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
        low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08519C",
        limits = c(0, max(pattern_scores, na.rm = TRUE)),
        name = "GeneFunnel score"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Broad-program score and calculation") +
    heatmap_theme +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9))
```

The coherent and dispersed samples each total 400. The coherent sample has only
small feature-to-feature differences, so its score remains close to 400. The
dispersed sample contains the same total in a mixture of high values and zeros;
its larger deviation penalty reduces the score to 165.6.

The uniformly high sample has no deviation and therefore scores its full total
of 800. The partial-observation sample contains five observed values of 80 and
five `NA` values. GeneFunnel omits the unavailable values, uses an effective
set size of five, and scores the observed total of 400. In contrast, the zeros
in the half-active and single-driver samples remain observed evidence. Half
activation receives partial credit, while one non-zero feature among nine zeros
gives the maximally dispersed score of zero.

# A narrower set can explain partial activity

The same panel can be scored against nested definitions. In the half-active
sample, every member of module A is measured at 80, while every member of module
B is zero.

```{r nested-sets}
nested_comparison <- data.frame(
    gene_set = rownames(pattern_scores),
    half_active_score = unname(pattern_scores[, "half_active"]),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    nested_comparison,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Gene set", "Score in half-active sample")
)

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
    nested_comparison$half_active_score,
    c(400, 0, 1600 / 9),
    tolerance = 1e-10
)))
```

```{r nested-score-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.cap=nested_cap}
pattern_observed <- t(vapply(pattern_sets, function(members) {
    colSums(!is.na(pattern_assay[members, , drop = FALSE]))
}, numeric(ncol(pattern_assay))))
pattern_score_cells <- matrix_cells(pattern_scores)
pattern_score_cells$observed <- as.vector(pattern_observed)
pattern_score_cells$label <- ifelse(
    is.na(pattern_score_cells$value),
    paste0("NA\nn = ", pattern_score_cells$observed),
    sprintf("%.1f\nn = %d", pattern_score_cells$value,
        pattern_score_cells$observed)
)
ggplot2::ggplot(pattern_score_cells,
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature, fill = value)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(label = label, colour = !is.na(value) & value > 450),
        size = 3.1
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "white"),
        guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = pattern_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = c(module_A = "Module A",
        module_B = "Module B", broad_program = "Broad program")) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
        low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08519C", na.value = "#E0E0E0",
        limits = c(0, max(pattern_scores, na.rm = TRUE)),
        name = "GeneFunnel score"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Feature matrix to gene-set matrix") +
    heatmap_theme +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9))

stopifnot(
    identical(dimnames(pattern_observed), dimnames(pattern_scores)),
    identical(is.na(pattern_scores), pattern_observed < 2),
    pattern_observed["module_B", "partial_observation"] == 0,
    pattern_observed["module_B", "half_active"] == 5
)
```

Module A scores its full total, module B scores zero, and the broader program is
penalized because only half of its members are active. This mirrors a useful
interpretive property of the method: a specific active module can explain a
partial signal better than an encompassing set. The sets should still be
predeclared. The example is not a reason to search adaptively for whichever
subset gives the largest score.

# Controlled gene-set perturbations

A second experiment separates two changes that can produce a higher score. It
starts from one synthetic sample and makes a modified copy. For the six-member
assembly set, the modified values are all set to their original mean. Its total
stays fixed while its within-set variation disappears. For the five-member
receptor set, every value increases by 40 while its variation stays unchanged.
Three background features are not members of either primary set.

```{r controlled-perturbations}
assembly_members <- paste0("assembly_", seq_len(6L))
receptor_members <- paste0("receptor_", seq_len(5L))
background_members <- paste0("background_", seq_len(3L))

original_values <- c(
    setNames(c(10, 25, 40, 55, 70, 100), assembly_members),
    setNames(c(28, 31, 30, 29, 32), receptor_members),
    setNames(c(18, 44, 65), background_members)
)
modified_values <- original_values
modified_values[assembly_members] <- mean(original_values[assembly_members])
modified_values[receptor_members] <-
    original_values[receptor_members] + 40

perturbation_assay <- cbind(
    original = original_values,
    modified = modified_values
)
perturbation_sets <- list(
    complex_assembly = assembly_members,
    receptor_activity = receptor_members,
    overlapping_response = c(
        assembly_members[5:6],
        receptor_members[1:3]
    )
)
perturbation_scores <- genefunnel(
    perturbation_assay,
    perturbation_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)

knitr::kable(
    perturbation_assay,
    digits = 0,
    col.names = c("Original", "Modified")
)
```

```{r perturbation-input-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5.5, fig.cap=perturb_input_cap}
perturbation_cells <- matrix_cells(perturbation_assay)
perturbation_modules <- setNames(
    rep(c("Assembly", "Receptor", "Background"), c(6L, 5L, 3L)),
    rownames(perturbation_assay)
)
perturbation_cells$module <- factor(
    perturbation_modules[as.character(perturbation_cells$feature)],
    levels = c("Assembly", "Receptor", "Background")
)
ggplot2::ggplot(perturbation_cells,
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature, fill = value)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.0f", value), colour = value > 60),
        size = 3.1
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = ggplot2::vars(module),
        scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "white"),
        guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = c(original = "Original", modified = "Modified")) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08519C",
        limits = c(0, max(perturbation_assay)), name = "Observed value") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Inspect the induced changes") +
    heatmap_theme
```

```{r controlled-perturbation-diagnostics}
perturbation_diagnostics <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(perturbation_sets), function(set_name) {
        members <- perturbation_sets[[set_name]]
        totals <- colSums(perturbation_assay[members, , drop = FALSE])
        scores <- perturbation_scores[set_name, ]

        data.frame(
            gene_set = set_name,
            sample = colnames(perturbation_assay),
            total = unname(totals),
            scaled_deviation = unname(totals - scores),
            genefunnel_score = unname(scores),
            check.names = FALSE
        )
    })
)
rownames(perturbation_diagnostics) <- NULL
knitr::kable(
    perturbation_diagnostics,
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
        "Gene set",
        "Sample",
        "Total",
        "Scaled deviation",
        "GeneFunnel score"
    )
)

stopifnot(
    identical(
        unname(colSums(perturbation_assay[assembly_members, ])),
        c(300, 300)
    ),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        unname(perturbation_scores["complex_assembly", ]),
        c(210, 300),
        tolerance = 1e-10
    )),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        unname(perturbation_scores["receptor_activity", ]),
        c(146.25, 346.25),
        tolerance = 1e-10
    ))
)
```

```{r perturb-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.2, fig.cap=perturb_cap}
perturbation_plot <- rbind(
    data.frame(
        gene_set = perturbation_diagnostics$gene_set,
        sample = perturbation_diagnostics$sample,
        metric = "Observed total",
        value = perturbation_diagnostics$total
    ),
    data.frame(
        gene_set = perturbation_diagnostics$gene_set,
        sample = perturbation_diagnostics$sample,
        metric = "GeneFunnel score",
        value = perturbation_diagnostics$genefunnel_score
    )
)
perturbation_plot$sample <- factor(
    perturbation_plot$sample,
    levels = c("original", "modified"),
    labels = c("Original", "Modified")
)
perturbation_plot$metric <- factor(
    perturbation_plot$metric,
    levels = c("Observed total", "GeneFunnel score")
)
perturbation_plot$gene_set <- factor(
    perturbation_plot$gene_set,
    levels = names(perturbation_sets),
    labels = c(
        "Complex assembly",
        "Receptor activity",
        "Overlapping response"
    )
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    perturbation_plot,
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = value, fill = metric)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(
        position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.72),
        width = 0.65
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(gene_set), nrow = 1) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
            "Observed total" = "#BDBDBD",
            "GeneFunnel score" = "#2C7FB8"
        ),
        name = NULL
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Value") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
            fill = "#F2F2F2",
            colour = NA
        ),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top"
    )
```

The assembly score rises from 210 to 300 without any change in its total. The
change is entirely due to greater coherence. The receptor score rises by 200
because its total rises by 200 and its deviation penalty remains 3.75. The
overlapping response also changes because it shares members with both modified
sets, but every set is still calculated independently.

```{r perturbation-membership-network, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap=membership_cap}
membership_edges <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(perturbation_sets), function(set) {
    data.frame(gene_set = set, member = perturbation_sets[[set]])
}))
membership_members <- unique(unlist(perturbation_sets, use.names = FALSE))
membership_y <- setNames(rev(seq_along(membership_members)), membership_members)
membership_set_y <- c(complex_assembly = 9, receptor_activity = 2,
    overlapping_response = 5.5)
membership_edges$y <- unname(membership_set_y[membership_edges$gene_set])
membership_edges$yend <- unname(membership_y[membership_edges$member])
membership_nodes <- data.frame(
    member = membership_members,
    y = unname(membership_y),
    shared = unname(table(membership_edges$member)[membership_members]) > 1L
)
membership_sets <- data.frame(
    gene_set = names(perturbation_sets),
    y = unname(membership_set_y[names(perturbation_sets)]),
    label = c("Complex assembly", "Receptor activity", "Overlapping response")
)
ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(data = membership_edges,
        ggplot2::aes(x = 0, xend = 1, y = y, yend = yend, colour = gene_set),
        linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.65) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = membership_sets,
        ggplot2::aes(x = 0, y = y, colour = gene_set), shape = 15, size = 5) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = membership_sets,
        ggplot2::aes(x = -0.05, y = y, label = label), hjust = 1, size = 3.3) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = membership_nodes,
        ggplot2::aes(x = 1, y = y, fill = shared), shape = 21, size = 3.5) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = membership_nodes,
        ggplot2::aes(x = 1.05, y = y, label = member,
            fontface = ifelse(shared, "bold", "plain")), hjust = 0, size = 3.2) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(complex_assembly = "#4477AA",
        receptor_activity = "#228833", overlapping_response = "#AA3377"),
        guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("#DDDDDD", "#CCBB44"), guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.85, 1.65), ylim = c(0.5, 11.5)) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Shared members connect independently scored sets",
        subtitle = "Declared memberships, not a biological interaction network") +
    ggplot2::theme_void(base_size = 11)

stopifnot(
    nrow(membership_edges) == sum(lengths(perturbation_sets)),
    sum(membership_nodes$shared) == 5L,
    !any(background_members %in% membership_edges$member),
    identical(perturbation_assay[background_members, "original"],
        perturbation_assay[background_members, "modified"])
)
```

This controlled design reflects two questions that appear in practical
analyses: did the members move together, and did their combined magnitude
change? GeneFunnel can register either effect in its sample-wise score. A
subsequent model is still required to estimate uncertainty or test differences
between biological groups.

# Real-data case study: presynaptic expression across Braak stages

The independent
[GSE125583](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE125583)
cohort accompanies
[Srinivasan et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.107843). It
contains processed bulk RNA-seq from fusiform gyrus tissue of 70 neurologically
normal controls and 219 autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer's disease subjects. GEO
records diagnosis, age, sex, and Braak stage; 287 of the 289 subjects have a
reported stage.

The per-sample processed tables contain size-factor-adjusted RPKM (`nRPKM`) and
raw counts. This vignette ships nRPKM values for all subjects and six genes:
`SYN1`, `SYN2`, `SYP`, `SNAP25`, `STX1A`, and `VAMP2`. The
`data-raw/build-gse125583-example.R` script regenerates the compact fixture from
checksum-verified GEO archives.

The synapsins and synaptophysin represent synaptic-vesicle organization, while
`SNAP25`, `STX1A`, and `VAMP2` form core presynaptic fusion machinery. The panel
was fixed for this vignette before inspecting its cohort-level association. It
is an illustrative panel, not a validated Alzheimer's disease signature or a
complete pathway.

Each gene is divided by its median nRPKM among the 70 control subjects before
scoring. This places the six positive trajectories on a common, non-negative
relative scale. GeneFunnel does not perform that preprocessing itself.

```{r gse125583-pipeline}
gse125583_path <- system.file(
    "extdata",
    "GSE125583_presynaptic_release.csv",
    package = "genefunnel"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(gse125583_path))
gse125583 <- utils::read.csv(
    gse125583_path,
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

presynaptic_genes <- c("SYN1", "SYN2", "SYP", "SNAP25", "STX1A", "VAMP2")
presynaptic_gene_ids <- c(
    SYN1 = 6853L,
    SYN2 = 6854L,
    SYP = 6855L,
    SNAP25 = 6616L,
    STX1A = 6804L,
    VAMP2 = 6844L
)
gse125583_expression <- t(as.matrix(gse125583[presynaptic_genes]))
colnames(gse125583_expression) <- gse125583$sample
storage.mode(gse125583_expression) <- "double"

control_columns <- gse125583$diagnosis == "control"
control_medians <- apply(
    gse125583_expression[, control_columns, drop = FALSE],
    1L,
    median
)
gse125583_relative <- sweep(
    gse125583_expression,
    1L,
    control_medians,
    "/"
)
gse125583_scores <- genefunnel(
    gse125583_relative,
    list(presynaptic_release = presynaptic_genes),
    BPPARAM = serial
)
presynaptic_total <- unname(colSums(gse125583_relative))
presynaptic_score <- unname(gse125583_scores["presynaptic_release", ])
braak_available <- !is.na(gse125583$braak)

gene_summary <- data.frame(
    gene = presynaptic_genes,
    entrez_gene_id = unname(presynaptic_gene_ids[presynaptic_genes]),
    control_median_nrpkm = unname(control_medians[presynaptic_genes]),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    gene_summary,
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c("Gene", "NCBI Gene ID", "Control median nRPKM")
)

association_summary <- data.frame(
    measure = c("Pearson correlation", "Spearman correlation"),
    six_gene_total = c(
        cor(
            presynaptic_total[braak_available],
            gse125583$braak[braak_available]
        ),
        cor(
            presynaptic_total[braak_available],
            gse125583$braak[braak_available],
            method = "spearman"
        )
    ),
    genefunnel_score = c(
        cor(
            presynaptic_score[braak_available],
            gse125583$braak[braak_available]
        ),
        cor(
            presynaptic_score[braak_available],
            gse125583$braak[braak_available],
            method = "spearman"
        )
    ),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    association_summary,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
        "Association with Braak stage",
        "Six-gene total",
        "GeneFunnel score"
    )
)
```

```{r gse-gene-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.7, fig.cap=gse_gene_cap}
braak_stages <- 1:6
braak_labels <- c("I", "II", "III", "IV", "V", "VI")
stage_gene_medians <- vapply(
    braak_stages,
    function(stage) {
        stage_columns <- which(gse125583$braak == stage)
        apply(
            gse125583_expression[, stage_columns, drop = FALSE],
            1L,
            median
        )
    },
    numeric(length(presynaptic_genes))
)
colnames(stage_gene_medians) <- braak_labels
stage_counts <- table(factor(gse125583$braak, levels = braak_stages))
stage_labels <- setNames(
    paste0(braak_labels, "\n(n=", as.integer(stage_counts), ")"), braak_labels
)
stage_minimum <- apply(stage_gene_medians, 1L, min)
stage_range <- apply(stage_gene_medians, 1L, max) - stage_minimum
stage_scaled <- 2 * sweep(
    sweep(stage_gene_medians, 1L, stage_minimum, "-"),
    1L, ifelse(stage_range > 0, stage_range, 1), "/"
) - 1
stage_scaled[stage_range == 0, ] <- 0

gse_raw_heatmap <- ggplot2::ggplot(matrix_cells(stage_gene_medians),
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature, fill = value)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = stage_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08519C",
        limits = c(0, max(stage_gene_medians)), name = "Median nRPKM") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Braak stage", y = NULL, title = "Unscaled abundance") +
    heatmap_theme +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8))
gse_scaled_heatmap <- ggplot2::ggplot(matrix_cells(stage_scaled),
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature, fill = value)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = stage_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
        midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Within-row range") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Braak stage", y = NULL, title = "Within-gene pattern") +
    heatmap_theme +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8))
draw_heatmap_pair(gse_raw_heatmap, gse_scaled_heatmap)

stopifnot(
    sum(stage_counts) == sum(braak_available),
    all(is.finite(stage_scaled)), all(abs(stage_scaled) <= 1),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        sweep(sweep((stage_scaled + 1) / 2, 1L, stage_range, "*"),
            1L, stage_minimum, "+"),
        stage_gene_medians, tolerance = 1e-12
    ))
)
```

The unscaled panel preserves abundance differences between genes. The companion
panel maps each gene's stage-median range to -1 through 1. It reveals direction
but removes between-gene magnitude information. A constant row would map to
zero. These display values never enter the scorer.

Each column summarizes different subjects, not repeated measurements of the
same people. The following figure retains individual scores and diagnosis
labels so that stage medians do not conceal subject-level variation.

```{r gse-score-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.4, fig.cap=gse_score_cap}
gse125583_score_plot <- data.frame(
    braak = factor(
        gse125583$braak[braak_available],
        levels = braak_stages,
        labels = braak_labels
    ),
    diagnosis = factor(
        gse125583$diagnosis[braak_available],
        levels = c("control", "Alzheimer's disease"),
        labels = c("Control", "Alzheimer's disease")
    ),
    score = presynaptic_score[braak_available],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
gse125583_score_medians <- stats::aggregate(
    score ~ braak,
    data = gse125583_score_plot,
    FUN = median
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    gse125583_score_plot,
    ggplot2::aes(x = braak, y = score)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        ggplot2::aes(colour = diagnosis, shape = diagnosis),
        position = ggplot2::position_jitter(
            width = 0.16,
            height = 0,
            seed = 1L
        ),
        alpha = 0.5,
        size = 1.8
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(
        data = gse125583_score_medians,
        ggplot2::aes(group = 1),
        colour = "#222222",
        linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        data = gse125583_score_medians,
        shape = 18,
        colour = "#222222",
        size = 2.8
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
        values = c(Control = "#4477AA", "Alzheimer's disease" = "#CC6677"),
        name = NULL
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
        values = c(Control = 16, "Alzheimer's disease" = 17),
        name = NULL
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Braak stage", y = "GeneFunnel score") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top"
    )
```

```{r gse125583-pipeline-check, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
    identical(dim(gse125583_expression), c(6L, 289L)),
    identical(
        as.integer(table(gse125583$diagnosis)[
            c("Alzheimer's disease", "control")
        ]),
        c(219L, 70L)
    ),
    sum(braak_available) == 287L,
    all(gse125583_expression > 0),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        control_medians,
        c(
            SYN1 = 119.521414801991,
            SYN2 = 53.495229040887,
            SYP = 230.823767700279,
            SNAP25 = 547.602073827910,
            STX1A = 68.824085690708,
            VAMP2 = 231.024436070715
        ),
        tolerance = 1e-10
    )),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        apply(
            gse125583_relative[, control_columns, drop = FALSE],
            1L,
            median
        ),
        stats::setNames(rep(1, 6), presynaptic_genes),
        tolerance = 1e-12
    )),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        presynaptic_score[c(1, 13, 101, 289)],
        c(
            3.11895741616489,
            5.76116235839454,
            5.17394506339094,
            7.02428095444394
        ),
        tolerance = 1e-10
    )),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        cor(
            presynaptic_score[braak_available],
            gse125583$braak[braak_available],
            method = "spearman"
        ),
        -0.4092210329,
        tolerance = 1e-10
    ))
)
```

Across the 287 subjects with a recorded stage, the GeneFunnel score has a
Spearman correlation of -0.409 with Braak stage; the plain six-gene total has a
correlation of -0.393. The stage-median score decreases from 6.39 at stage I to
1.93 at stage VI, although adjacent stages are not strictly monotonic.
GeneFunnel's contribution is the sample-specific disagreement penalty, not a
claim that this compact panel has a materially stronger pathology association
than its sum.

The result is descriptive. Braak stage and diagnosis are closely related in
this autopsy cohort, and the calculation does not adjust for age, sex, technical
variation, or tissue cell composition. It also does not fit or test an
association. A full analysis should predeclare a complete gene set and
preprocessing plan, assess coverage, and use an appropriate downstream model.
The six-gene panel is an inspectable scoring example, not a biomarker.

# Real-data scale study: mouse brain cell types

The presynaptic case study makes every member inspectable, but its six-gene
panel does not demonstrate scoring at larger set sizes. The
[GSE60361](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE60361)
experiment from
[Zeisel et al. (2015)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaa1934) profiled 3,005
single cells from juvenile mouse somatosensory cortex and CA1 hippocampus.

The compact fixture contains all 19,972 endogenous genes aggregated into 47
named cell-subtype profiles. These profiles represent 2,816 cells in seven
broad classes. Aggregation reduces single-cell sparsity and makes each column a
pseudobulk profile. The fixture-generation script retrieves the versioned
`zeisel-brain-2015` resource through `scRNAseq::ZeiselBrainData()`.

Counts are converted to counts per million (CPM). The seven broad-class
profiles define an equal-class abundance reference. Genes with a positive
median CPM across those profiles are ranked by that median, with gene name as a
deterministic tie-breaker. The top 5,000 genes form the larger panel, and the
top 500 form the nested smaller panel. Each subtype CPM is divided by the
corresponding broad-class median before scoring. These are abundance-defined
scale panels, not pathways or cell-type signatures.

```{r gse60361-scale-pipeline}
gse60361_path <- system.file(
    "extdata",
    "GSE60361_brain_cell_types.rds",
    package = "genefunnel"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(gse60361_path))
gse60361 <- readRDS(gse60361_path)
gse60361_subtype_counts <- gse60361$subtype_counts
gse60361_broad_counts <- gse60361$broad_class_counts

gse60361_broad_cpm <- sweep(
    gse60361_broad_counts,
    2L,
    colSums(gse60361_broad_counts) / 1e6,
    "/"
)
gse60361_reference <- apply(
    gse60361_broad_cpm,
    1L,
    median
)
gse60361_eligible_rows <- which(
    is.finite(gse60361_reference) &
    gse60361_reference > 0
)
gse60361_abundance_order <- gse60361_eligible_rows[
    order(
        -gse60361_reference[gse60361_eligible_rows],
        rownames(gse60361_broad_counts)[gse60361_eligible_rows]
    )
]
gse60361_5000_genes <- rownames(gse60361_broad_counts)[
    gse60361_abundance_order[seq_len(5000L)]
]
gse60361_gene_sets <- list(
    `500-gene panel` = gse60361_5000_genes[seq_len(500L)],
    `5,000-gene panel` = gse60361_5000_genes
)

gse60361_subtype_cpm <- sweep(
    gse60361_subtype_counts,
    2L,
    colSums(gse60361_subtype_counts) / 1e6,
    "/"
)
gse60361_relative <- sweep(
    gse60361_subtype_cpm[
        gse60361_5000_genes,
        ,
        drop = FALSE
    ],
    1L,
    gse60361_reference[gse60361_5000_genes],
    "/"
)
gse60361_scores <- genefunnel(
    gse60361_relative,
    gse60361_gene_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)
gse60361_totals <- t(vapply(
    gse60361_gene_sets,
    function(members) {
        colSums(gse60361_relative[members, , drop = FALSE])
    },
    numeric(ncol(gse60361_relative))
))
```

Absolute GeneFunnel scores are not directly comparable across panel sizes
because the formula includes the member sum. Dividing the total and score by
panel size supports this display without changing the calculation. The
retained fraction is the score divided by the observed total.

```{r gse60361-scale-summary, echo=FALSE}
gse60361_class_order <- c(
    "pyramidal CA1",
    "pyramidal SS",
    "interneurons",
    "oligodendrocytes",
    "astrocytes_ependymal",
    "microglia",
    "endothelial-mural"
)
gse60361_class_labels <- c(
    "pyramidal CA1" = "CA1 pyramidal",
    "pyramidal SS" = "Somatosensory pyramidal",
    interneurons = "Interneurons",
    oligodendrocytes = "Oligodendrocytes",
    astrocytes_ependymal = "Astrocytes / ependymal",
    microglia = "Microglia",
    `endothelial-mural` = "Endothelial / mural"
)
gse60361_subtype_metadata <- gse60361$subtype_metadata
gse60361_sample_scores <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(gse60361_gene_sets), function(panel_name) {
        members <- gse60361_gene_sets[[panel_name]]
        totals <- unname(gse60361_totals[panel_name, ])
        scores <- unname(gse60361_scores[panel_name, ])

        data.frame(
            panel = panel_name,
            genes = length(members),
            subtype = gse60361_subtype_metadata$subtype,
            broad_class = gse60361_subtype_metadata$broad_class,
            cells = gse60361_subtype_metadata$cells,
            total_per_gene = totals / length(members),
            score_per_gene = scores / length(members),
            retained_fraction = scores / totals,
            check.names = FALSE,
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
    })
)
rownames(gse60361_sample_scores) <- NULL
gse60361_sample_scores$class_label <- factor(
    gse60361_sample_scores$broad_class,
    levels = gse60361_class_order,
    labels = unname(gse60361_class_labels[gse60361_class_order])
)

gse60361_panel_summary <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(gse60361_gene_sets), function(panel_name) {
        panel_scores <- gse60361_sample_scores[
            gse60361_sample_scores$panel == panel_name,
            ,
            drop = FALSE
        ]

        data.frame(
            panel = panel_name,
            genes = panel_scores$genes[[1L]],
            median_total = median(panel_scores$total_per_gene),
            median_score = median(panel_scores$score_per_gene),
            median_retained = median(panel_scores$retained_fraction),
            minimum_retained = min(panel_scores$retained_fraction),
            maximum_retained = max(panel_scores$retained_fraction),
            check.names = FALSE,
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
    })
)
rownames(gse60361_panel_summary) <- NULL
gse60361_class_summary <- stats::aggregate(
    retained_fraction ~ panel + broad_class,
    data = gse60361_sample_scores,
    FUN = median
)
gse60361_class_summary$class_label <- unname(
    gse60361_class_labels[gse60361_class_summary$broad_class]
)

gse60361_500_summary <- gse60361_panel_summary[
    gse60361_panel_summary$panel == "500-gene panel",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
gse60361_5000_summary <- gse60361_panel_summary[
    gse60361_panel_summary$panel == "5,000-gene panel",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
gse60361_500_classes <- gse60361_class_summary[
    gse60361_class_summary$panel == "500-gene panel",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
gse60361_5000_classes <- gse60361_class_summary[
    gse60361_class_summary$panel == "5,000-gene panel",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
gse60361_500_low <- gse60361_500_classes[
    which.min(gse60361_500_classes$retained_fraction),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
gse60361_500_high <- gse60361_500_classes[
    which.max(gse60361_500_classes$retained_fraction),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
gse60361_5000_low <- gse60361_5000_classes[
    which.min(gse60361_5000_classes$retained_fraction),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
gse60361_5000_high <- gse60361_5000_classes[
    which.max(gse60361_5000_classes$retained_fraction),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]

gse60361_panel_display <- data.frame(
    panel = gse60361_panel_summary$panel,
    genes = format(
        gse60361_panel_summary$genes,
        big.mark = ",",
        scientific = FALSE,
        trim = TRUE
    ),
    median_total = sprintf(
        "%.3f",
        gse60361_panel_summary$median_total
    ),
    median_score = sprintf(
        "%.3f",
        gse60361_panel_summary$median_score
    ),
    median_retained = sprintf(
        "%.1f",
        100 * gse60361_panel_summary$median_retained
    ),
    retained_range = sprintf(
        "%.1f-%.1f",
        100 * gse60361_panel_summary$minimum_retained,
        100 * gse60361_panel_summary$maximum_retained
    ),
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    gse60361_panel_display,
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    col.names = c(
        "Panel",
        "Genes",
        "Median total/gene",
        "Median score/gene",
        "Median retained (%)",
        "Retained range (%)"
    )
)
```

## Results across panel sizes

Across the 47 subtype profiles, the 500-gene panel has a median total per gene
of `r sprintf("%.3f", gse60361_500_summary$median_total)` and a median score per
gene of `r sprintf("%.3f", gse60361_500_summary$median_score)`. The median
retained fraction is
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * gse60361_500_summary$median_retained)`%. Across broad
classes, the median retained fraction ranges from
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * gse60361_500_low$retained_fraction)`% for
`r gse60361_500_low$class_label` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * gse60361_500_high$retained_fraction)`% for
`r gse60361_500_high$class_label`.

With the nested panel expanded tenfold, the 5,000-gene panel has a median total
per gene of
`r sprintf("%.3f", gse60361_5000_summary$median_total)` and a median score per
gene of `r sprintf("%.3f", gse60361_5000_summary$median_score)`. Its median
retained fraction is
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * gse60361_5000_summary$median_retained)`%. Broad-class
medians range from
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * gse60361_5000_low$retained_fraction)`% for
`r gse60361_5000_low$class_label` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * gse60361_5000_high$retained_fraction)`% for
`r gse60361_5000_high$class_label`.

```{r gse60361-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap=gse60361_cap}
gse60361_plot <- gse60361_sample_scores
gse60361_plot$panel <- factor(
    gse60361_plot$panel,
    levels = names(gse60361_gene_sets)
)
gse60361_palette <- stats::setNames(
    c(
        "#4477AA",
        "#66CCEE",
        "#228833",
        "#CCBB44",
        "#EE6677",
        "#AA3377",
        "#666666"
    ),
    levels(gse60361_plot$class_label)
)
gse60361_shapes <- stats::setNames(
    c(16, 17, 15, 18, 8, 3, 4),
    levels(gse60361_plot$class_label)
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    gse60361_plot,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = total_per_gene,
        y = score_per_gene,
        colour = class_label,
        shape = class_label
    )
) +
    ggplot2::geom_abline(
        slope = 1,
        intercept = 0,
        colour = "#8C8C8C",
        linetype = "dotted"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2.4) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(panel), nrow = 1) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
        values = gse60361_palette,
        name = "Broad class"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
        values = gse60361_shapes,
        name = "Broad class"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
        x = "Observed total per gene",
        y = "GeneFunnel score per gene"
    ) +
    ggplot2::guides(
        colour = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
        shape = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
            fill = "#F2F2F2",
            colour = NA
        ),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top"
    )
```

```{r gse60361-class-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap=class_heatmap_cap}
gse60361_class_counts <- table(gse60361_subtype_metadata$broad_class)
gse60361_class_plot <- gse60361_class_summary
gse60361_class_plot$panel <- factor(gse60361_class_plot$panel,

gse60361_class_plot$broad_class <- factor(gse60361_class_plot$broad_class,

ggplot2::ggplot(gse60361_class_plot,

stopifnot(
    sum(gse60361_class_counts) == ncol(gse60361_scores),

```

```{r gse60361-scale-check, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
    identical(gse60361$source$accession, "GSE60361"),
    identical(gse60361$source$dataset, "zeisel-brain-2015"),
    identical(gse60361$source$dataset_version, "2023-12-14"),
    identical(dim(gse60361_subtype_counts), c(19972L, 47L)),
    identical(dim(gse60361_broad_counts), c(19972L, 7L)),
    typeof(gse60361_subtype_counts) == "integer",
    typeof(gse60361_broad_counts) == "integer",
    all(gse60361_subtype_counts >= 0L),
    all(gse60361_broad_counts >= 0L),
    sum(gse60361$subtype_metadata$cells) == 2816L,
    length(gse60361_eligible_rows) >= 5000L,
    identical(
        head(gse60361_5000_genes, 10L),
        c(
            "Malat1",
            "Tmsb4x",
            "Meg3",
            "Ppia",
            "Actb",
            "Calm1",
            "Hsp90aa1",
            "App",
            "Hsp90ab1",
            "Fth1"
        )
    ),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        unname(gse60361_reference[
            gse60361_5000_genes[c(500L, 5000L)]
        ]),
        c(230.58259149905, 33.4246588837642),
        tolerance = 1e-10
    )),
    identical(
        unname(vapply(gse60361_gene_sets, length, integer(1L))),
        c(500L, 5000L)
    ),
    all(gse60361_gene_sets[[1L]] %in% gse60361_gene_sets[[2L]]),

    isTRUE(all.equal(
        unname(gse60361_scores[
            ,
            c("Astro1", "Oligo3", "S1PyrL5")
        ]),
        matrix(
            c(
                474.815372360286,
                4100.74526146677,
                411.536717685261,
                3380.13217420648,
                458.474356781014,
                5154.6619950742
            ),

    ))
)
```

Every point lies below the identity line because the deviation penalty is
non-negative. In this abundance-defined display, neuronal subtype profiles tend
to retain a larger share of their totals than glial profiles. That pattern is
descriptive and depends on the panel construction and scaling reference. It is
not a cell-type enrichment test. Pseudobulk aggregation also removes
within-subtype cell variation. The example demonstrates the score mechanics at
500 and 5,000 genes rather than validated biological programs.

# Choosing between GeneFunnel and rank-based methods

Gene-set scoring is already supported by several complementary packages.
[`GSVA`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/GSVA) offers unsupervised gene-set
transformations whose methods use relative expression or rank information.
[`singscore`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/singscore) and
[`UCell`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/UCell) calculate single-sample
scores from within-sample feature ranks, with UCell using a Mann-Whitney U
statistic.

GeneFunnel answers a different question. It does not rank values or estimate a
distribution across samples. Instead, it applies the formula above to each set
and sample independently. The score therefore depends on measurement scale,
set size, and observed coverage. Choose the method that matches the quantity
you want to preserve.

# Check coverage before scoring

A declared member absent from the matrix changes global assay coverage. It is
different from a missing cell, which affects only one sample, and from an
observed zero. `gene_set_coverage()` exposes these facts before scoring.

```{r coverage}
catalogue <- list(
    complete_module = rownames(pattern_assay)[1:5],
    partial_catalogue = c("gene_A", "gene_B", "gene_C", "gene_K"),
    duplicated_members = c("gene_A", "gene_A", "gene_B"),
    insufficient = c("gene_A", "gene_Z")
)
coverage <- gene_set_coverage(catalogue, rownames(pattern_assay))
knitr::kable(
    coverage,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
        "Gene set",
        "Declared",
        "Matched",
        "Unmatched",
        "Coverage",
        "Duplicates",
        "Scoreable"
    )
)
```

GeneFunnel can score a set whenever at least two unique members match. It does
not impose a coverage fraction because suitable thresholds depend on the
experiment. A transcriptomic analysis might require complete coverage:

```{r strict-coverage}
strict <- !is.na(coverage$coverage) & coverage$coverage == 1
names(catalogue[strict])
```

A low-coverage proteomic analysis might require at least 50% coverage and at
least two matched members:

```{r relaxed-coverage}
relaxed <- !is.na(coverage$coverage) &
    coverage$coverage >= 0.5 &
    coverage$matched_size >= 2
names(catalogue[relaxed])

relaxed_scores <- genefunnel(
    pattern_assay,
    catalogue[relaxed],
    BPPARAM = serial
)
knitr::kable(
    relaxed_scores,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
        "Coherent",
        "Same total, dispersed",
        "Uniform high",
        "Partial observation",
        "Half active",
        "Single driver"
    )
)
```

These thresholds are examples rather than package recommendations. Record the
gene-set collection, its version, and the threshold used in the analysis.

# Dense and sparse matrices

Sparse input stays sparse through scoring, and implicit zeros remain observed.
Stored sparse `NA` and `NaN` values follow the same sample-specific omission
rule as dense missing values.

```{r sparse}
pattern_sparse <- Matrix::Matrix(pattern_assay, sparse = TRUE)
pattern_sparse_scores <- genefunnel(
    pattern_sparse,
    pattern_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)

isTRUE(all.equal(
    pattern_sparse_scores,
    pattern_scores,
    tolerance = 0,
    check.attributes = TRUE
))
```

The dense and sparse implementations are required to produce the same named
matrix. Sparse storage changes memory use and traversal, not the scientific
calculation.

# Serial and parallel execution

`BPPARAM` accepts any suitable `BiocParallelParam`. `SerialParam()` is useful
for debugging and small inputs. A portable SOCK backend can distribute bounded
column chunks while preserving sample order.

```{r parallel}
sock <- BiocParallel::bpstart(BiocParallel::SnowParam(
    workers = 2L,
    type = "SOCK",
    progressbar = FALSE
))
parallel_scores <- tryCatch(
    genefunnel(pattern_assay, pattern_sets, BPPARAM = sock),
    finally = BiocParallel::bpstop(sock)
)

identical(parallel_scores, pattern_scores)
```

Process startup and data transfer can outweigh parallel work on small inputs.
Benchmark the intended workload rather than assuming that more workers are
faster.

# Identifiers and preprocessing

Matrix row names and gene-set names must be unique, non-missing, and non-empty.
Member matching is exact, with no case conversion, synonym resolution, or
annotation lookup. Duplicated members within one set are counted in coverage
diagnostics and deduplicated for scoring. Overlapping sets remain valid and do
not influence one another.

GeneFunnel requires non-negative input with a meaningful zero. It applies no
automatic preprocessing. An arbitrary positive shift is unsuitable because
adding a constant $c$ to all $n$ observed members adds $nc$ to the score. Raw
non-negative measurements can be preferable when scientifically appropriate,
but the package does not prescribe a universal pipeline position.

# Interpretation and limitations

The absolute-deviation penalty treats within-set variability as evidence
against coherent activity. That is a scientific assumption rather than a
universal property of biological pathways.

The sum term preserves magnitude and therefore also preserves effects of input
units, library size, preprocessing, set size, and feature coverage. Independent
sample scoring does not make scores from unrelated data sets automatically
comparable. Such comparisons require compatible units, preprocessing,
identifiers, gene-set definitions, versions, and coverage policies.

Gene-set database revisions can change scores. The package does not guarantee
that the resulting distribution meets the assumptions of every downstream
statistical method. Validate those assumptions for the intended analysis.

The full scoring specification is installed as `SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md`:

```{r specification-path}
specification <- system.file("SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md", package = "genefunnel")
stopifnot(nzchar(specification), file.exists(specification))
basename(specification)
```
